quarterly_data.signal: REC-4881 (oral MEK1/2 inhibitor, FAP), Chief Development Officer Vicki Goodman: in the ongoing Phase II TUPELO study, post-colectomy FAP patients receiving REC-4881 showed a median polyp burden reduction of 43% after three months of treatment; the effect was durable, with sustained reductions after three months off treatment, and reductions were seen in both duodenal (upper GI) and lower GI disease - approximately 90% of FAP patients develop upper GI polyps. The safety profile is manageable with predominantly mild to moderate adverse events, consistent with other MEK inhibitors. TUPELO continues to enroll, including patients 18 years of age and older and a dose optimization cohort. The data were first presented in December via a webinar; she said FDA engagement focuses on de-risking the study design, including the appropriate primary endpoint, given very limited regulatory precedent in FAP.
quarterly_data.figure: median polyp burden reduction of 43% after three months; approximately 90% of FAP patients develop upper GI polyps

quarterly_data.signal: REC-7735 (PI3K-alpha H1047R inhibitor), Vicki Goodman: the IND is now cleared by FDA and Recursion intends to initiate the Phase I ZINNIA trial later this year - dose escalation in patients with PIK3CA-H1047R mutant solid tumors, then expansion into a hyperglycemia-vulnerable patient cohort once tolerability is confirmed at an active dose, then dose optimization of two active and tolerated doses in ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer; first data from the dose-escalation part are expected in the first half of 2028. REC-7735 is designed to be greater than 100-fold selective for H1047R; the go decision rested on preclinical efficacy similar to or improved on competitor profiles, lack of hyperglycemia and GLP tox studies. She sees potential expansion to diabetic and prediabetic patients, other PIK3CA-mutant tumors (e.g. triple-negative breast, ovarian, endometrial cancer) and non-oncology PI3K-driven vascular anomalies.
quarterly_data.figure: IND cleared; Phase I start later this year; first dose-escalation data in the first half of 2028; greater than 100-fold selectivity for H1047R
